name.en: Tech support pop-up: “your computer is infected, call this number”

how.en: A pop-up appears on your computer saying it has a virus or a security problem, and uses the name of a company like Microsoft, Apple or Geek Squad. It tells you to call a phone number right away. The person who answers says your device is infected, asks to get into your computer, and sells you a fake fix or support plan. Real tech companies’ security warnings never ask you to call a phone number. Tech support scams were one of the costliest scams reported to the FBI in 2025, with over $2.1 billion in losses.

text.en: A pop-up or warning screen says your computer is infected or hacked.
It tells you to call a number now and not to turn off your computer.
The “technician” asks you to install a program so they can see your screen.
They charge you for a fake repair or support plan, or ask for card or bank details.

WINDOWS SECURITY ALERT: Your computer has been blocked due to suspicious activity. Your personal data is at risk. Do not close this window or restart your computer. Call Microsoft Support immediately.

en: pop-up said my computer was infected
technician took control of my computer
screen said don't turn off computer
A pop-up with a phone number to call about a virus.
Warnings not to close the window or restart your computer.
A stranger asking for remote access to your computer.
A fee for a repair or support plan you didn’t ask for.
Don’t call the number or click links in the pop-up. Close the browser, or restart the computer.
Update your security software and run a scan yourself.
If you need help, contact a company you trust using the details on its official website, or a store you know.
If you let someone in, run a security scan, change your passwords and call your bank or card issuer.

sources.title: Seemingly urgent security messages could lead to tech support scams
